title: Stranger Anxiety: A New Kind of Wary
hook: Around 6 to 9 months, a once-sociable baby may suddenly turn shy or cry around unfamiliar people — even doting grandparents. It's a normal sign their mind and memory are growing.
key_points: Stranger anxiety commonly appears around 6–9 months and reflects new abilities: telling familiar from unfamiliar and preferring trusted people.
It's different from separation anxiety — this is wariness of unfamiliar people, even when you're right there.
Don't force it: let new people approach slowly, stay close, and let your baby warm up on their own timeline.
It's a normal, passing phase that eases over the following months as your baby's world widens.
content_html: Somewhere around six to nine months, a baby who used to smile at everyone can become suddenly shy — burying their face, fussing, or crying when an unfamiliar person comes close, sometimes even with grandparents or a familiar babysitter. It can feel like a step backward or a worry about the baby's mood, but it's actually a developmental leap: your baby can now tell the difference between the people they know well and everyone else, and they've decided they have a strong preference.
extra_html: It helps to know this is distinct from separation anxiety. Stranger anxiety is about unfamiliar people — your baby may protest a new face even while sitting safely in your arms. The kindest response is not to push it: let new people hang back and approach slowly, keep your baby near you, and let them set the pace for warming up. A familiar voice, a favorite toy, and your calm presence all reassure them. Like separation anxiety, it's a phase, and it eases over the following months as your baby grows more comfortable with a wider world. This is general educational information — mention it to your pediatrician if it seems unusually intense or long-lasting.

related.title: Separation Anxiety: A Sign of a Strong Bond
related.hook: When your baby melts down the moment you leave, it's not a setback — it's a normal phase and a sign of healthy attachment. Brief, confident goodbyes and a consistent ritual help.

related.title: Soothing a Fussy Newborn
related.hook: Newborns are wired to be calmed by sensations that echo the womb — holding, swaddling, gentle motion, white noise, and sucking. One rule overrides all: never, ever shake a baby.

flashcards.prompt: What does stranger anxiety around 6–9 months usually signal?

choices.text: Normal development — the baby can now tell familiar from unfamiliar people
That the baby has been spoiled by too much holding
A social problem that needs evaluation

flashcards.explanation_html: Stranger anxiety is a healthy milestone: it shows a baby now distinguishes familiar caregivers from unfamiliar people and prefers the people they trust.

flashcards.prompt: How is stranger anxiety different from separation anxiety?
flashcards.back_html: Stranger anxiety is wariness of unfamiliar people, even with you right there. Separation anxiety is distress when you leave. Both are normal phases.
